topIssues.title: Remove IFaultDisputeGame dependency from AnchorStateRegistry
topIssues.author: ajsutton
topIssues.body: The `AnchorStateRegistry` currently assumes games implement the `IFaultDisputeGame` interface. With interop (and ZK) this is no longer true.  We should ensure `AnchorStateRegistry` only uses `IDisputeGame`. We can add additional methods to `IDisputeGame` if needed but should review to ensure they really are necessary.

topIssues.title: op-batcher: Make blob tip cap mechanism configurable
topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
The batcher (or rather its included txmgr) currently only allows to set a static _tip cap_ (or _maximum priority fee_). It also already contains a module that is tracking the distribution of tip caps of the most recent blob transactions and that can calculate (and currently emit on a metric) a certain percentile of this distribution (currently fixed at 0.6).

To make better decisions about blob tip caps, the batcher should now be enabled to use this blob tip cap tracker as a source for its tip cap in new transactions. It should still be possible to select a static tip cap, so using the new dynamic mechanism should be configurable. Furthermore, the percentile to use should also be configurable, with a default value of `0.6`.

topPRs.title: feat(flashblocks): enable speculative building on pending blocks (3)
topPRs.author: teddyknox
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Enable building flashblocks on top of pending blocks before their canonical parent arrives via P2P, reducing latency when flashblocks arrive faster than canonical blocks.

Part of the [speculative flashblock building design](https://www.notion.so/oplabs/Flashblocks-Upstreaming-node-reth-features-2e8f153ee162805eaaa5f067fe3440a3?source=copy_link). Builds on [PR 2](https://github.com/op-rs/op-reth/pull/591), and will rebase to target https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth once it merges.

## Motivation

The sequence manager currently discards flashblocks whose parent hash doesn't match the canonical tip. This means flashblocks for block N+1 sit idle until block N propagates via P2P—negating the latency advantage of the WebSocket feed.

With speculative building, we track execution state from previous builds and use it as prestate for subsequent builds, allowing continuous flashblock processing without waiting for P2P.

## Changes

**`pending_state.rs`** (new)
- `PendingBlockState<N>` - Tracks block hash, number, parent hash, execution outcome, and cached reads from a build
- `PendingStateRegistry<N>` - Stores most recent pending state for use by subsequent builds

**`cache.rs`**
- Extend `next_buildable_args()` with 3-priority build selection:
  1. Canonical-Pending: pending sequence parent matches canonical tip
  2. Canonical-Cached: cached sequence parent matches canonical tip  
  3. Speculative: pending/cached sequence parent matches pending state's block hash
- Add `pending_parent` field to `BuildArgs`

**`worker.rs`**
- Accept optional `pending_parent` in `BuildArgs`
- Use `with_bundle_prestate()` to overlay pending state's bundle on the canonical state provider
- Return `PendingBlockState` in `BuildResult` for use by subsequent builds

**`service.rs`**
- Add `PendingStateRegistry` field
- Record pending state after successful builds
- Pass pending state to `next_buildable_args()`
- Clear pending states on reconciliation
- Add `with_speculative_building()` opt-in (disabled by default)

## Testing

New integration test harness in `tests/it/`:
- `harness.rs` - `FlashBlockServiceTestHarness`, `TestSequenceManager`, `TestFlashBlockFactory`
- `service.rs` - Tests for speculative build priority, canonical precedence, pending state registry, depth limits

topPRs.title: feat: skip protocol versions deployment when opcmv2 enabled
topPRs.author: 0xniha
topPRs.body:
# Description
This PR deprecates the `ProtocolVersions` contract when OPCM v2 is enabled via the dev feature bitmap.
When OPCM v2 is active, the system now:
- Skips deployment of `ProtocolVersionsProxy` and `ProtocolVersionsImpl` contracts.
- Validates that all protocol versions-related fields are set to zero addresses/values.
- Detects OPCM v2 from the dev feature bitmap in the deployment pipeline.
- Maintains backwards compatibility with OPCM v1 (which continues to use `ProtocolVersions` as before).

topPRs.title: feat(flashblocks): add validation module for sequence ordering and reorg detection (1)
topPRs.author: teddyknox
topPRs.body:
Part of the [speculative flashblock building design](https://www.notion.so/oplabs/Flashblocks-Upstreaming-node-reth-features-2e8f153ee162805eaaa5f067fe3440a3?source=copy_link).

## Motivation

The existing flashblocks implementation relies on implicit parent hash matching to reject invalid sequences, but lacks explicit detection of sequence gaps, duplicates, and reorgs. This PR adds the foundational validation types that subsequent PRs will use for canonical block reconciliation and speculative building.

## Changes

Adds `validation.rs` with three stateless validators:

- **`FlashblockSequenceValidator`** - Validates that incoming flashblocks follow expected ordering. Returns `NextInSequence`, `FirstOfNextBlock`, `Duplicate`, `NonSequentialGap`, or `InvalidNewBlockIndex`.

- **`ReorgDetector`** - Compares transaction hash slices between tracked pending state and canonical blocks. Returns `NoReorg` or `ReorgDetected` with diagnostic counts.

- **`CanonicalBlockReconciler`** - Determines reconciliation strategy when canonical blocks arrive: `CatchUp`, `HandleReorg`, `DepthLimitExceeded`, `Continue`, or `NoPendingState`.

All types are stateless with `const fn` where possible, making them easy to test and reason about.

## Testing

Comprehensive unit tests covering:
- Sequence validation: consecutive indices, block transitions, gaps, duplicates
- Reorg detection: matching sequences, different order, different counts, different hashes
- Reconciliation: all strategy branches and priority ordering
